newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks weighed down by more profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks weighed down by more profit-taking.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks languished in negative territory Tuesday, hampered by profit-taking and a softer bond market, while technology stocks rallied anew as investors focused on corporate earnings.
At 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT), the Dow Jones industrial average was off 25.55 points at 7,897.43.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 14-12 on heavy volume of 328 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
But the Nasdaq composite index, continued to outpace the Dow index, added 7.66 points to 1,531.54 amid the gains in tech stocks.

A steady stream of second-quarter earnings set the tune for various stock sectors, while investors kept an eye on the bond market and a surging dollar, which was hovering around six-year peaks against the German mark.

"Each company seems to dancing to its own earnings-reporting tune," said Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp. "Some are dancing to a waltz and others to a funeral dirge. ... The volatility game continues."
But despite many solid reports, the Dow was locked in a consolidation mode after it failed to receive a needed boost from bonds, analysts said.
"The Dow is moving sideways here," said Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics. "It is not receiving any help from the fixed-income market."

The benchmark 30-year Treasury fell 5/32, or $1.5625 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.57 percent to 6.55 percent Monday, following the release of retail sales data, which rose 0.5 percent in June, the first increase in four months.
"The economic data was relatively constructive," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management division.
"But our belief is that, regardless of the tone of economic data, the long bond is running into resistance at the 6.50 percent level," he said.
Analysts said stocks needed support from bonds to continue to rally, because many were trading at such high valuations.
"Stocks basically need a favourable fixed-income environment to perform," Ellis said. "It seems like rates have fallen so far that the next move can only be up."

While a stronger dollar could hurt corporate profits of multinational companies doing business abroad, it would mostly serve to attract foreign investors to U.S. stocks in the near term, analysts said.
The dollar was trading near a six-year high of 1.8031 German marks.
Technology stocks look beyond the bond market, optimistically awaiting earnings from bellwether companies like Intel Corp. and Microsoft Corp.
Chip maker Intel, which was expected to report its second quarter results after Tuesday's close, was up 1-1/2 at 80-1/4 in active trade.
"The stock is acting reasonably well," said Jim Benning, trader at BT Brokerage. "I think everyone is hoping for the best here."
Texas Instruments Inc. surged 11-1/4 to 108-3/4, after it reported unexpectedly strong second quarter income.
Merrill Lynch had second quarter net earnings of $481 million, the highest of any quarter in the firm's history. Its stock gained 1-15/16 to 65-5/8.
